items.setupText: Choose the form that describes Mina's usual journey now.
items.taskText: Mina ___ the bus to work every day.
items.explanation: Takes is present simple: it describes Mina's usual journey. Add -s with she or a person's name.

rationales.take: With Mina, the present simple needs takes, with -s.
rationales.took: Took describes a past journey or past habit, not her usual journey now.
rationales.takes: Takes is present simple: it describes Mina's usual journey. Add -s with she or a person's name.
rationales.is taking: Is taking presents an activity in progress or a temporary arrangement, not the usual routine requested.

findings: Original routine allowed an unstated temporary interpretation and offered only generic feedback.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Links a regular journey to present simple and singular agreement.

items.setupText: Choose the form for a finished time in the past.
items.taskText: The bank ___ closed yesterday.
items.explanation: Was is the past form of is for one bank. Yesterday identifies the past time.

rationales.is: Is describes the bank now; yesterday places this statement in the past.
rationales.was: Was is the past form of is for one bank. Yesterday identifies the past time.
rationales.be: Be cannot stand alone here; use the past form was.
rationales.are: Are is present tense and goes with a plural subject, not the bank.

findings: Original repeated the Yesterday plus action-verb frame without diagnostic feedback.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that states as well as actions have past forms.
audit.levelReason: Was and yesterday are basic past-time foundations.
audit.similarityNote: Describes a bank's state rather than a completed action.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: I don't ___ coffee.
items.explanation: After don't, use the base form drink. Don't carries the present-tense negative.

rationales.drink: After don't, use the base form drink. Don't carries the present-tense negative.
rationales.drinks: Don't already supplies the helping verb; the next verb does not take -s.
rationales.drank: Drank is a past form. After don't, use drink.
rationales.drinking: Drinking needs a different construction, such as am not drinking.

findings: Original duplicated another morning routine and misdescribed agreement errors as time errors.
audit.microSkill: Base form after don't
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates the negative helping verb from the main verb.
audit.levelReason: A personal preference and a basic negative suit A1.
audit.similarityNote: Tests first-person present negation, not a positive routine.

items.setupText: Choose the form that shows an action happening now.
items.taskText: Please wait. The hotel workers ___ your bags now.
items.explanation: Are carrying shows the workers doing the action now. The continuous form uses be plus an -ing verb.

rationales.carried: Carried presents the action as past, not happening as you wait.
rationales.carry: Carry can describe their job or routine; it does not present this action as in progress.
rationales.has carried: Has carried presents completed carrying and uses singular has, but hotel workers is plural.
rationales.are carrying: Are carrying shows the workers doing the action now. The continuous form uses be plus an -ing verb.

findings: Original was another isolated Yesterday item with identical wrong-answer messages.
audit.microSkill: Present continuous for action in progress
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a request to wait with an unfinished action.
audit.levelReason: Bags and waiting provide a concrete beginner context.
audit.similarityNote: Uses an immediate service interaction rather than a habit.

items.setupText: Choose the form for a completed trip yesterday.
items.taskText: Omar ___ to the market yesterday.
items.explanation: Went is the past form of go. It describes Omar's completed trip yesterday.

rationales.goes: Goes is present tense; the trip happened yesterday.
rationales.went: Went is the past form of go. It describes Omar's completed trip yesterday.
rationales.going: Going alone is not a complete verb after Omar.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches went in a practical travel statement.
audit.levelReason: A common irregular verb with explicit yesterday is suitable for A1.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct question.
items.taskText: Ask about Lena's location now.
items.explanation: Where is Lena? puts the present form is before the subject in a direct question.

rationales.Where does Lena is?: Do not add does when is is the main verb; ask Where is Lena?
rationales.Where is Lena?: Where is Lena? puts the present form is before the subject in a direct question.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows the question order for a current location.
audit.levelReason: A short where question is a beginner communication need.
audit.similarityNote: Changes the response demand to selecting a whole question.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: Sofia doesn't ___ on Sundays.
items.explanation: Use work after doesn't. The -s belongs to does, not to the main verb.

rationales.works: Doesn't carries the singular present marking, so the main verb stays work.

rationales.work: Use work after doesn't. The -s belongs to does, not to the main verb.

findings: Original was a noun-swapped morning routine with interchangeable feedback.
audit.microSkill: Base form after doesn't
audit.pedagogicalValue: Targets double marking of third-person present tense.
audit.levelReason: Work schedules make a familiar A1 negative statement.
audit.similarityNote: Contrasts with the don't item through singular does support.

items.setupText: Choose the form for a finished action last night.
items.taskText: We ___ a film last night.
items.explanation: Watched uses -ed for a completed past action. Last night gives the finished time.

rationales.watched: Watched uses -ed for a completed past action. Last night gives the finished time.
rationales.watch: Watch is present tense with we; this sentence describes last night.
rationales.watches: Watches is present tense for he, she, or it, not a past action with we.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a common leisure event to the regular past ending.
audit.levelReason: Simple vocabulary and an explicit past time suit A1.
audit.similarityNote: Uses a plural subject and leisure setting for regular past.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: I ___ waiting outside your building.

rationales.is: Is goes with he, she, or it; I needs am.
rationales.be: The base form be cannot follow I alone in this present statement.
rationales.am: I takes am. Am waiting is the present continuous form for an action in progress.

audit.microSkill: Am as a continuous auxiliary
audit.pedagogicalValue: Builds a complete present continuous message with I.

audit.similarityNote: Focuses on the helping verb rather than choosing an action's tense.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: Did you ___ the door?
items.explanation: Did marks the question as past, so the main verb remains lock.

rationales.locked: Did already marks past time; use lock, not locked, after it.
rationales.locking: Locking cannot follow did in this question.

rationales.lock: Did marks the question as past, so the main verb remains lock.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that says where Hana lives now.
items.taskText: Hana moved to Seoul last year. Seoul is still her home.

Lives states Hana's present home. Present simple can describe a current state.

items.setupText: Choose the form that describes last Monday.
items.taskText: Jonas ___ at work last Monday; he was at home.
items.explanation: Wasn't means was not. It denies a past location and matches he was at home.

rationales.wasn't: Wasn't means was not. It denies a past location and matches he was at home.

rationales.not was: Put not after was: was not, or wasn't.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines past location with a clear negative correction.
audit.levelReason: Wasn't and familiar locations provide A1 past foundations.
audit.similarityNote: The only A1 contrast between two past locations.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: I'll ___ you tomorrow.
items.explanation: I'll means I will. Will is followed by the base form call.

rationales.called: After will, use the base form call, not the past form called.
rationales.calling: Calling would need be after will: I'll be calling.
rationales.calls: Calls cannot follow will; the verb after will has no -s.
rationales.call: I'll means I will. Will is followed by the base form call.

findings: Original's repeated finding-a-file routine added little distinct learning value.
audit.microSkill: Base form after will
audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches the form of a simple future promise.
audit.levelReason: A short promise with tomorrow is a suitable future foundation.
audit.similarityNote: Introduces will through a common contracted message.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: They ___ cooking dinner.
items.explanation: Aren't means are not. Use it with they before cooking for a negative continuous statement.

rationales.isn't: Isn't takes a singular subject; they needs aren't.
rationales.aren't: Aren't means are not. Use it with they before cooking for a negative continuous statement.
rationales.doesn't: Doesn't cannot come directly before an -ing verb and does not agree with they.
rationales.don't: Don't goes with a base verb, as in don't cook, not directly with cooking.

findings: Original was another irregular-past office/classroom item with boilerplate feedback.
audit.microSkill: Negative plural present continuous
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes aren't cooking from don't cook.
audit.levelReason: A short dinner sentence and common negatives suit A1.
audit.similarityNote: Combines plural agreement with continuous negation.

items.setupText: Choose the form for a present-day fact.
items.taskText: My phone ___ two cameras.
items.explanation: Has describes what one phone possesses now. Use has with it.

rationales.have: With one phone, the present form is has, not have.
rationales.having: Having alone cannot be the complete verb in this statement.
rationales.has: Has describes what one phone possesses now. Use has with it.

audit.microSkill: Present possession with has
audit.pedagogicalValue: Practises an irregular present form in a useful object description.
audit.levelReason: A phone and a small number keep the demand at A1.
audit.similarityNote: Covers possession rather than a routine or an ongoing action.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: What time does the class ___?
items.explanation: Does is followed by the base form start in a present-simple question.

rationales.start: Does is followed by the base form start in a present-simple question.
rationales.starts: Does already carries the singular -s marking; do not add -s to start.
rationales.started: Started is a past form, but does requires the base form.
rationales.starting: Starting cannot directly follow the subject after does in this question.

audit.microSkill: Does in a present-time question
audit.pedagogicalValue: Builds a practical question about a class schedule.
audit.levelReason: Asking a start time is a basic A1 task.
audit.similarityNote: A wh-question about a schedule, unlike the be location question.

items.setupText: Choose the answer that matches the past-time question.
items.taskText: Were you and Emma late yesterday? No, we ___.
items.explanation: Weren't matches both we and the past helping verb were in the question.

rationales.aren't: Aren't answers about the present; the question uses were and yesterday.
rationales.wasn't: Wasn't does not agree with we; the plural past form is weren't.
rationales.don't: Don't answers a question with do, not one with were.
rationales.weren't: Weren't matches both we and the past helping verb were in the question.

audit.microSkill: Past be in a plural short answer
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows how a short answer repeats the question's tense.
audit.levelReason: A brief late/not-late exchange suits A1 interaction.
audit.similarityNote: The A1 short-answer task, with a plural past subject.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: We are going to ___ a room near the station.
items.explanation: Use rent after are going to. This construction describes a plan.

rationales.rented: Going to takes a base verb, not the past form rented.
rationales.rent: Use rent after are going to. This construction describes a plan.
rationales.renting: Here to is followed by rent, not renting.
rationales.rents: Rents cannot follow going to; the planned action uses the base form.

audit.microSkill: Base form in going-to plans
audit.pedagogicalValue: Forms a simple accommodation plan.
audit.levelReason: A basic going-to plan is a foundation for beginner future reference.
audit.similarityNote: Practises going to separately from the will promise.

items.setupText: Choose the statement about an action happening now.
items.taskText: Yara is on the phone at this moment.

She is talking to her sister.
She called her sister last night.
She will call her sister tomorrow.
items.answer: She is talking to her sister.
items.explanation: Is talking describes an action in progress at this moment.

Every week describes a routine, not this call in progress.
Last night places that call in the past.
Is talking describes an action in progress at this moment.
Tomorrow places the call in the future, not at this moment.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a complete continuous sentence to a current situation.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
items.taskText: Theo didn't ___ breakfast today.
items.explanation: After didn't, use the base form eat. Didn't marks the negative as past.

rationales.eat: After didn't, use the base form eat. Didn't marks the negative as past.

rationales.eaten: Eaten is used with have or be, not directly after didn't.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes eat, ate, and eaten in a past negative.

items.setupText: Choose the form that presents this as a temporary situation.
items.taskText: Our office is being painted, so I ___ from home this week.

rationales.am working: Am working presents the home-working arrangement as temporary during the painting.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a future plan from experience and routine.

items.setupText: Choose the form showing an activity already in progress when the phone rang.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.

rationales.knew: Knew locates the knowledge in the past; the request relies on his knowledge now.
rationales.is knowing: For an existing state of knowledge in neutral standard English, use knows rather than is knowing.
rationales.will know: Will know predicts or infers knowledge; the task asks for a direct statement of his present knowledge.
rationales.knows: Knows describes a present state of knowledge. This sense of know normally uses the simple form.

findings: Original was a repeated Tomorrow teaching frame without useful distractor diagnosis.

items.setupText: Choose the forms for two completed events in this past account.
items.taskText: Sara ___ her bags and then ___ a taxi.
items.explanation: Packed and called present two completed past events; then gives their order.

rationales.packs / calls: These present forms could narrate a story in the present, but the task requests a past account.
rationales.packed / called: Packed and called present two completed past events; then gives their order.
rationales.has packed / calls: This mixes a present-perfect result with a present routine and does not form the requested past sequence.
rationales.was packing / is calling: These continuous forms mix past and present and do not state two completed past events.

findings: Original Right now bringing item added only a noun change to the set.
audit.microSkill: Simple past in a sequence
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows consistent past narration across two linked events.
audit.levelReason: A short travel sequence makes an A2 two-verb choice manageable.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence using present continuous for a future arrangement.
items.taskText: Luis and Ana have agreed to meet at six tomorrow.
options: Luis is meeting Ana at six.
Luis has met Ana at six.
Luis was meeting Ana at six.
items.answer: Luis is meeting Ana at six.
items.explanation: Is meeting is present continuous. With the given future context, it expresses an agreed arrangement.

Met places the meeting in the past rather than the agreed future.
Has met looks back at an earlier meeting; it does not state the arrangement for tomorrow.
Is meeting is present continuous. With the given future context, it expresses an agreed arrangement.
Was meeting gives a past viewpoint, not Luis's current arrangement for tomorrow.

findings: Original Tomorrow beginning repeated the going-to item pattern.
audit.microSkill: Present continuous for arrangements
audit.pedagogicalValue: Explains future reference in a form also used for current actions.
audit.levelReason: An agreed meeting and a clear time support A2 use.
audit.similarityNote: A social appointment, separate from a published train timetable.

items.setupText: Choose the form meaning the task is still unfinished now.
items.taskText: My assistant started the registration form this morning, but she ___ it yet.
items.explanation: Hasn't finished with yet means completion has not happened by the present time.

rationales.won't finish: Won't finish predicts a future outcome or expresses refusal; it does not directly report progress up to now.
rationales.isn't finishing: Isn't finishing says the finishing activity is not happening, not whether completion has occurred by now.
rationales.doesn't finish: Doesn't finish usually describes a habit or regular result, not this unfinished form up to now.
rationales.hasn't finished: Hasn't finished with yet means completion has not happened by the present time.

findings: Original Right now completing was repetitive and supplied no useful meaning contrast.
audit.microSkill: Negative present perfect with yet
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reports an expected action that remains incomplete now.
audit.levelReason: A familiar form and a clear starting time suit A2.
audit.similarityNote: Focuses on absence of completion rather than a positive present result.

items.setupText: Choose the question about the length of Noah's continuing stay.
items.taskText: Noah arrived in this city in June and is still here.
options: How long has Noah been here?
items.answer: How long has Noah been here?
items.explanation: Has Noah been links his arrival to now, and how long asks for the duration of the continuing stay.

rationales.How long has Noah been here?: Has Noah been links his arrival to now, and how long asks for the duration of the continuing stay.
rationales.When will Noah be here?: When will asks about a future time, but Noah is already here.
rationales.How long was Noah here?: Was asks about a past stay viewed as a past period, not his stay continuing now.
rationales.When is Noah coming here?: Is coming asks about an arrival arrangement, not how long the current stay has lasted.

findings: Original Tomorrow explaining item repeated future recognition and generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: How long with present perfect be
audit.pedagogicalValue: Forms a useful duration question about a continuing situation.
audit.levelReason: Arrival and current residence provide a clear A2 timeline.
audit.similarityNote: Asks for duration, whereas Mateo's job item supplies a starting point.

items.setupText: Choose the pair that presents a usual routine and a temporary change.
items.taskText: My aunt usually ___ lunch at home, but this week she ___ at the cafe.
items.explanation: Eats gives the usual routine; is eating presents this week's change as temporary.

rationales.is eating / eats: This reverses the requested perspectives: continuous for the usual routine and simple for the temporary change.
rationales.ate / has eaten: This describes past eating and experience up to now, not a present routine with a temporary change.
rationales.eats / is eating: Eats gives the usual routine; is eating presents this week's change as temporary.
rationales.has eaten / ate: These forms look back at earlier eating rather than contrasting a current routine and a temporary change.

findings: Original Right now comparing frame was a further copy of the level's repeated pattern.
audit.microSkill: Simple versus continuous across a contrast
audit.pedagogicalValue: Coordinates tense choices across two clauses with different time perspectives.
audit.levelReason: Lunch habits and one temporary week support an A2 comparison.
audit.similarityNote: Requires two coordinated choices rather than the single temporary-work form.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that reports a completed move two years before now.
items.taskText: Theo wants to say when he moved to this apartment.
options: I move here in two years.
I moved here two years ago.
I have moved here for two years.
I am moving here in two years.
items.answer: I moved here two years ago.
items.explanation: Moved with two years ago reports a completed event at a measured distance before now.

In two years points forward, not two years before now.
Moved with two years ago reports a completed event at a measured distance before now.
For two years expresses duration, but this completed move is an event with a past date.
Am moving with in two years describes a future arrangement, not the completed move.

findings: Original ended with another Tomorrow office-action frame and identical feedback.
audit.microSkill: Simple past with ago
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a past event's date from duration and future distance.
audit.levelReason: Explaining when one moved is an accessible A2 biographical task.
audit.similarityNote: Uses a relative past date, distinct from Lena's calendar-year purchase.

items.setupText: Choose the form reporting a total completed between Monday and now.
items.taskText: It's Thursday. Since Monday, Mina ___ three job applications.
items.explanation: Has sent counts completed applications within a period that reaches the present Thursday.

rationales.is sending: Is sending describes an activity in progress rather than the total already completed.
rationales.has sent: Has sent counts completed applications within a period that reaches the present Thursday.
rationales.sends: Sends describes a routine, not an accumulated total since Monday.
rationales.had sent: Had sent counts back from a past reference point; this total is measured up to now.

findings: Original was a repeated Since Monday/twice frame with generic rationales.
audit.microSkill: Present perfect for a completed count
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes results accumulated so far from activity in progress.
audit.levelReason: Counting achievements over an unfinished period is suitable B1 work.
audit.similarityNote: An explicit Thursday reporting point anchors a completed count.

items.setupText: Choose the standard form in this future time clause.
items.taskText: I'll meet you outside when your bus ___ tomorrow.
items.explanation: After when in a future time clause, present simple can refer to tomorrow: when your bus arrives.

rationales.arriving: Arriving alone does not provide a complete verb after your bus.
rationales.will arrive: Will arrive works in a main prediction. In this standard future time clause after when, use the present form arrives.
rationales.arrived: Arrived puts the arrival in the past rather than in this open future arrangement.
rationales.arrives: After when in a future time clause, present simple can refer to tomorrow: when your bus arrives.

findings: Original incorrectly excluded has checked from an if clause where it was a valid alternative.
audit.microSkill: Present simple in future time clauses
audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches future reference without will in a time clause.
audit.levelReason: Linking a future plan to an arrival event is a B1 clause-level choice.
audit.similarityNote: Uses a time clause, not the ambiguous original condition.

items.setupText: Choose the form emphasizing an activity that began earlier and is continuing now.
items.taskText: Aiko started practicing at nine. It's eleven and she is still at the piano: she ___ for two hours.
items.explanation: Has been practicing looks back over two hours of activity that continues at the present time.

rationales.has been practicing: Has been practicing looks back over two hours of activity that continues at the present time.
rationales.had practiced: Had practiced measures earlier practice from a past viewpoint, not from the present eleven o'clock.
rationales.will practice: Will practice describes future practice, not the two hours already underway.
rationales.practices: Practices can state a routine of two-hour sessions; it does not express this continuing session from nine until now.

findings: Original repeated the same Since Monday completed-count item with a different verb.
audit.microSkill: Present perfect continuous for ongoing duration
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes duration of activity from a count of finished results.
audit.levelReason: Interpreting a start time, current time, and continuing activity fits B1.
audit.similarityNote: A timed practice session contrasts with Mina's completed applications.

items.setupText: Choose the form that explicitly places the departure before my arrival.
items.taskText: When I reached the station, Nadia ___; her train was already on its way.
items.explanation: Had left places Nadia's departure before another past event, my arrival at the station.

rationales.was leaving: Was leaving would put departure in progress at my arrival, not already over.
rationales.has left: Has left relates departure to now, but the reference point is my past arrival.
rationales.had left: Had left places Nadia's departure before another past event, my arrival at the station.
rationales.is leaving: Is leaving gives a present viewpoint rather than the past sequence described.

findings: Original rejected a legitimate has sent condition and used generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Past perfect for earlier past completion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Makes the order of two past events explicit.
audit.levelReason: A clear travel narrative supports an introductory B1 past-perfect contrast.
audit.similarityNote: An already departed train supplies evidence for earlier completion.

items.setupText: Choose the ordinary tense for this finished biographical period.
items.taskText: My grandfather, who died in 2006, ___ as a chef for forty years.
items.explanation: Worked presents the forty-year career within a finished life period. For can accompany simple past when the period is over.

rationales.has worked: Has worked connects a work history to a present period; this sentence explicitly closes his life and career in the past.
rationales.worked: Worked presents the forty-year career within a finished life period. For can accompany simple past when the period is over.
rationales.is working: Is working presents current work, which conflicts with the stated death.
rationales.will work: Will work places the career in the future, contrary to this completed biography.

findings: Original repeated a present-perfect count and reduced every error to a vague time mismatch.
audit.microSkill: Simple past for a finished duration
audit.pedagogicalValue: Counters the mistaken rule that for always requires present perfect.
audit.levelReason: A biographical duration requires B1 attention to the whole context.
audit.similarityNote: Tests duration in a closed life period rather than a continuing activity.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation of the present perfect in this condition.
items.taskText: If you've already paid online, you won't need to pay at the door.
options: Earlier online payment removes the need to pay at the door.
Online payment will begin at the door.
Online payment is no longer possible.
items.answer: Earlier online payment removes the need to pay at the door.
items.explanation: You've already paid refers to payment completed before the relevant check. Present perfect is valid in an if clause.

Already paid refers to completed payment, not payment beginning at the door.
The sentence says nothing about whether online payment remains available.
If leaves it open whether a particular person has paid; it does not claim everyone has.
rationales.Earlier online payment removes the need: You've already paid refers to payment completed before the relevant check. Present perfect is valid in an if clause.

findings: Original falsely rejected has prepared in a conditional; the new item directly addresses that misconception.
audit.microSkill: Present perfect in an open condition
audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches a legitimate completed-action condition without inventing a ban on perfect forms.
audit.levelReason: Interpreting an everyday admission condition fits B1 comprehension.
audit.similarityNote: A meaning question explicitly rehabilitates the original wrongly rejected construction.

items.setupText: Choose the form describing a past state that is no longer true.
items.taskText: Before the supermarket was built, this corner ___ a small bakery.
items.explanation: Used to have describes the former state of this corner and implies a change since then.

rationales.used to have: Used to have describes the former state of this corner and implies a change since then.
rationales.would having: Would cannot be followed by having; for this former state, used to have is the natural construction.
rationales.has had: Has had looks back from now rather than locating this state wholly before the supermarket was built.
rationales.is having: Is having presents a current activity and does not express this former state of possession.

findings: Original repeated Since Monday printing and supplied no diagnostic explanations.
audit.microSkill: Used to with a past state
audit.pedagogicalValue: Extends used to beyond repeated actions to former situations.
audit.levelReason: Describing neighborhood change is a B1 narrative function.
audit.similarityNote: A former state contrasts with the lower-level discontinued cycling habit.

items.setupText: Choose the form presenting an activity in progress at a future time.
items.taskText: Don't call at eight tomorrow evening. I ___ an online class then.
items.explanation: Will be attending places the class in progress at the future time when the call would interrupt it.

rationales.attended: Attended describes past attendance, not tomorrow evening.
rationales.have attended: Have attended reports experience or completion before now.
rationales.will be attending: Will be attending places the class in progress at the future time when the call would interrupt it.
rationales.had attended: Had attended looks back from a past point rather than forward to tomorrow.

findings: Original's has opened condition was grammatical but rejected without justification.
audit.microSkill: Future continuous at a specified moment
audit.pedagogicalValue: Explains future unavailability through an activity in progress.
audit.levelReason: A future appointment with an interruption context supports B1 aspect choice.
audit.similarityNote: The B1 future activity viewed from inside its duration.

items.setupText: Choose the pair that links a continuing situation to its past starting event.
items.taskText: Rina ___ much happier since she ___ jobs last autumn.
items.explanation: Has been connects her happiness to now; changed names the finished past event that began that period.

rationales.was / has changed: Was does not establish the continuing present situation, and has changed does not fit the dated starting event last autumn.
rationales.is being / changes: Is being suggests current behavior rather than a continuing state; changes does not locate the job change last autumn.
rationales.had been / changes: Had been needs a past reference point, while changes is present rather than the stated past starting event.
rationales.has been / changed: Has been connects her happiness to now; changed names the finished past event that began that period.

findings: Original repeated a simple present-perfect count without varying the decision.
audit.microSkill: Present perfect main clause with past since clause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that linked clauses can need different tenses.
audit.levelReason: Coordinating a continuing state and its dated cause is B1 work.
audit.similarityNote: Tests both sides of since rather than merely recognizing the word.

items.setupText: Choose the completion meaning Mateo is still away at the pharmacy.
items.taskText: Mateo isn't here. He ___ to the pharmacy.
items.explanation: Has gone to the pharmacy presents his departure as resulting in his current absence.

rationales.has gone: Has gone to the pharmacy presents his departure as resulting in his current absence.
rationales.has been: Has been to normally reports a completed visit, often with a return, so it does not express the requested still-away meaning.
rationales.was going: Was going reports a past journey in progress or intention without establishing where he is now.
rationales.used to go: Used to go describes a discontinued habit, not today's absence.

findings: Original rejected has read in a valid if clause and supplied only boilerplate feedback.
audit.microSkill: Has gone versus has been
audit.pedagogicalValue: Links present-perfect word choice to whether a visitor has returned.
audit.levelReason: Explaining someone's absence is a common B1 practical distinction.
audit.similarityNote: The current location consequence of gone, distinct from loss or discovery.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that emphasizes a recent activity without saying the job is finished.
items.taskText: A decorator has paint on her hands. Some of the wall is still bare.
options: The decorator has painted the whole wall.
The decorator painted the wall last year.
The decorator has been painting the wall.
The decorator will paint the wall tomorrow.
items.answer: The decorator has been painting the wall.
items.explanation: Has been painting focuses on recent activity with visible evidence now and does not claim the wall is finished.

rationales.The decorator has painted the whole wall: The whole wall makes a completion claim that conflicts with the bare section.
rationales.The decorator painted the wall last year: Last year's work does not describe the recent activity indicated by her hands.
rationales.The decorator has been painting the wall: Has been painting focuses on recent activity with visible evidence now and does not claim the wall is finished.
rationales.The decorator will paint the wall tomorr: Tomorrow describes future work rather than the activity responsible for the current paint on her hands.

findings: Original repeated choosing a topic twice with a generic explanation of perfect tense.
audit.microSkill: Perfect continuous for recent activity and evidence
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates evidence of activity from a claim of completion.
audit.levelReason: Drawing a supported inference from a familiar scene fits B1.
audit.similarityNote: Recent visible evidence, unlike the still-continuing piano session.

items.setupText: Choose the pair that expresses a current opinion and a decision being considered now.
items.taskText: I ___ this flat is too small, so I ___ about moving.
items.explanation: Think states an opinion; am thinking about describes the ongoing process of considering a move.

rationales.am thinking / think: This reverses the intended uses: the opinion takes think, while active consideration takes am thinking.
rationales.think / am thinking: Think states an opinion; am thinking about describes the ongoing process of considering a move.
rationales.thought / have thought: Thought places the opinion in the past, and have thought looks back on consideration rather than presenting it as underway now.
rationales.had thought / thought: Both forms locate thinking in the past, not in the two present meanings requested.

findings: Original repeated an if frame that allowed the rejected has made alternative.
audit.microSkill: State and activity senses of think
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows how a verb's meaning affects simple or continuous choice.
audit.levelReason: Distinguishing opinion from active consideration adds B1 semantic demand.
audit.similarityNote: The B1 state/activity verb-sense contrast.

items.setupText: Choose the form expressing an intention that existed before the interruption.
items.taskText: I ___ the curtains, but the shop closed before I got there.
items.explanation: Was going to buy reports a past intention. The shop's closure explains why this planned purchase did not happen then.

rationales.have bought: Have bought says the purchase has happened, not that an earlier intention was interrupted.
rationales.am buying: Am buying presents a current arrangement or activity rather than the earlier plan.
rationales.buy: Buy describes a present routine or narrative action, not the past intention requested.
rationales.was going to buy: Was going to buy reports a past intention. The shop's closure explains why this planned purchase did not happen then.

audit.microSkill: Was going to for a past intention
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes planning an action from carrying it out.
audit.levelReason: An everyday interrupted plan supports B1 future-in-the-past meaning.
audit.similarityNote: The B1 unrealized shopping intention.

items.setupText: Choose the form comparing today's experience with all earlier experience up to now.
items.taskText: This is the quietest hotel I ___ at.
items.explanation: Have ever stayed compares this hotel with the speaker's experience up to the present.

rationales.have ever stayed: Have ever stayed compares this hotel with the speaker's experience up to the present.
rationales.will ever stay: Will ever stay extends the claim into the future, beyond the earlier experience requested.
rationales.had ever stayed: Had ever stayed requires a past comparison point, as in That was the quietest hotel I had ever stayed at.
rationales.am ever staying: Am ever staying does not form an experience comparison across previous visits.

audit.microSkill: Present perfect in an experiential superlative
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a present evaluation to a lifetime comparison.
audit.levelReason: Using an experience clause after a superlative is B1 sentence-level practice.
audit.similarityNote: A present hotel evaluation rather than a direct ever question.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that says the repair was completed before the call.

Sara repaired the bike after the customer called.
Sara would repair the bike after the customer called.
Sara had repaired the bike when the customer called.

items.explanation: Had repaired presents the repair as complete by the past time of the call.

audit.microSkill: Reconstructing a past sequence from two statements
audit.pedagogicalValue: Checks the consequences of tense choice for event order.
audit.levelReason: Combining two time statements into one is a B1 narrative skill.
audit.similarityNote: A whole-sentence timeline choice rather than the station gap fill.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation of the future instruction.
items.taskText: Don't switch off the computer until it has saved the file.

Wait until someone starts editing the file.

audit.microSkill: Present perfect for completion in a future time clause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that present perfect need not describe only events before speech time.
audit.levelReason: Understanding a practical ordered instruction fits B1.
audit.similarityNote: A future prerequisite, distinct from already-paid conditions about earlier action.

items.setupText: Choose the form reporting a future promise from a past viewpoint.
items.taskText: On Monday, the guide promised that she ___ me the address the following day.

rationales.had sent: Had sent places sending before the promise, reversing the intended order.
rationales.sends: Sends is present simple and does not express this future promise viewed from Monday.
rationales.would send: Would send looks forward from the past promise to the following day; it is the reported counterpart of will send.

findings: Original repeated a completed application count with formulaic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Would as future from a past reporting point
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes reported promises from earlier completed events.
audit.levelReason: Reporting a simple promise is suitable B1 indirect-speech practice.

items.setupText: Choose the forms for a life-experience question followed by a dated answer.
items.taskText: '___ you ever visited Lisbon?' 'Yes, I ___ there in 2022.'

audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows why a conversation can appropriately change from present perfect to simple past.
audit.levelReason: Managing tense across an experience exchange is B1 discourse practice.
audit.similarityNote: A two-speaker exchange with a justified tense shift.

items.setupText: Choose the form presenting the chef's residence as the background already in progress.
items.taskText: The chef ___ in Madrid when she met her future business partner.

rationales.has lived: Has lived connects residence to now rather than presenting background at the past meeting.
rationales.will live: Will live points forward from now, not to residence at that past time.
rationales.was living: Was living sets the chef's residence as an ongoing background situation when the meeting occurred.
rationales.had lived: Had lived looks back on residence from a past point; it does not give the requested in-progress view of residence at the meeting.

findings: Original was another repeated present-perfect count of workplace comparisons.
audit.microSkill: Past continuous for a background situation
audit.pedagogicalValue: Extends past continuous beyond an action interrupted at one instant.
audit.levelReason: A biographical setting for a meeting is a B1 narrative choice.
audit.similarityNote: An extended residence rather than the shorter interrupted dinner activity.

items.setupText: Choose the form emphasizing sustained activity leading up to a past decision.

rationales.had been arguing: Had been arguing emphasizes the duration of the argument leading up to the past decision to take a break.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects sustained earlier activity with a later past decision.

rationales.will have delivered: Will have delivered looks back from next Friday at a delivery already completed by then.

rationales.had delivered: Had delivered looks back from a past point, not from next Friday.
