items.explanation: Knew is a modal past: it presents current personal familiarity as an imagined state rather than a past event.

rationales.knew: Knew is a modal past: it presents current personal familiarity as an imagined state rather than a past event.
rationales.had met: Had met would describe an imagined earlier meeting, not the requested current state of knowing someone; met him personally changes the target meaning.
rationales.will know: Will know places familiarity in the future, not in the imagined current relationship.
rationales.has met: Has met presents an earlier meeting without the requested remote present-state form and changes knowledge to meeting.

findings: Original future-perfect forms item was a repeated basic pattern with an unjustified rejected will print.
audit.microSkill: Modal past in an as-if current-state comparison
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes imagined present familiarity from earlier events.
audit.levelReason: Separating remote tense from chronology in a comparison is C1 interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: An as-if comparison about a current relationship.

items.setupText: Choose the pair preserving both the simultaneous job and the earlier resignation in the report.
items.taskText: In March, Daniel said he ___ for a charity and that he ___ from the bank the previous December.
items.explanation: Was working reports the work underway at the March conversation; had resigned places the bank resignation earlier, in December.

rationales.had worked / is resigning: Had worked places charity work before the reporting point, while is resigning does not express the completed December resignation.
rationales.is working / will resign: Will resign makes the resignation later, contrary to the previous December; is working also changes the requested past reporting viewpoint.
rationales.was working / had resigned: Was working reports the work underway at the March conversation; had resigned places the bank resignation earlier, in December.
rationales.would work / has resigned: Would work makes charity work prospective, and has resigned shifts the completed resignation to a present viewpoint.

findings: Original's opening the office for two hours was unnatural and repeated an under-specified duration choice.
audit.microSkill: Simultaneity and anteriority within a past report
audit.pedagogicalValue: Assigns different past forms to events with different relations to the reporting time.
audit.levelReason: Tracking two embedded events around a shared reporting point is C1 work.
audit.similarityNote: A two-part employment report with March and December anchors.

items.setupText: Choose the statement emphasizing a recent recurring pattern still relevant now, without presenting a settled policy.
items.taskText: Several clients have complained about delays during the last few weeks.
options: Support staff have been taking several days to answer requests.
Support staff answered requests within a day last year.
Support staff will answer requests within several days next year.
Support staff had answered the requests before the complaints began.
items.answer: Support staff have been taking several days to answer requests.
items.explanation: Have been taking presents repeated delays over a recent period without making them a permanent rule.

rationales.Support staff answered requests within a: Last year's response time does not describe the recent pattern behind these complaints.
rationales.Support staff have been taking several d: Have been taking presents repeated delays over a recent period without making them a permanent rule.
rationales.Support staff will answer requests withi: Next year's prediction does not characterize the recent delays already reported.
rationales.Support staff had answered the requests: Had answered describes earlier completion, not a recurring recent pattern of slow responses.

findings: Original future-perfect answers item was repetitive and rejected a grammatical will answer deadline reading.
audit.microSkill: Perfect continuous for a recent recurring pattern
audit.pedagogicalValue: Applies progressive aspect to repeated bounded actions across a period.
audit.levelReason: Expressing a provisional pattern from several instances is C1 reporting practice.
audit.similarityNote: Repeated response delays, not one continuous task.

items.setupText: Choose the inference supported by the whole account, not by 'had hoped' alone.
items.taskText: 'We had hoped to finish before lunch, but a missing part kept us there until six.'
options: The intended lunch deadline was missed, as the later clause confirms.
The hope itself began only after the work finished.
The work had already finished when the hope was formed.
The past perfect guarantees that the missing part was later found.
items.answer: The intended lunch deadline was missed, as the later clause confirms.
items.explanation: The 'but' clause establishes the missed deadline. 'Had hoped' supplies the earlier expectation, which alone would not prove disappointment.

rationales.The hope itself began only after the wor: 'Had hoped' places the hope before the later outcome, not after the work ended.
rationales.The work had already finished when the h: 'Hoping to finish' treats completion as prospective from the earlier hope.
rationales.The past perfect guarantees that the mis: 'Had hoped' does not establish what happened to the missing part.
rationales.The intended lunch deadline was missed,: The 'but' clause establishes the missed deadline. 'Had hoped' supplies the earlier expectation, which alone would not prove disappointment.

findings: Original accepted only had been reading although was reading and had read allowed coherent readings.
audit.microSkill: Earlier expectation versus contextually established failure
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a tense's contribution from an inference licensed by surrounding text.
audit.levelReason: Evaluating the source of an implied outcome is a C1 reading decision.
audit.similarityNote: A missed expectation whose failure is supplied by an explicit later clause.

items.setupText: Choose the form explicitly emphasizing accumulated ongoing activity at a future anniversary.
items.taskText: When the arts center celebrates its tenth anniversary next June, its director ___ the evening classes for eight years.
items.explanation: Will have been coordinating looks back from next June over eight years of an activity continuing at that future point.

rationales.will have been coordinating: Will have been coordinating looks back from next June over eight years of an activity continuing at that future point.
rationales.had been coordinating: Had been coordinating looks back from a past point, not the future anniversary.
rationales.will begin coordinating: Will begin coordinating starts the activity then rather than accumulating eight years by then.
rationales.has been coordinating: Has been coordinating measures duration up to now, not up to next June.

findings: Original's next-Friday choosing frame supplied a basic form contrast and allowed will choose.
audit.microSkill: Future perfect continuous across a long duration
audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines a future reference point with accumulated ongoing work.
audit.levelReason: Managing duration relative to a future milestone supports C1 aspect control.
audit.similarityNote: A future anniversary measures a long-running repeated role.

items.setupText: Choose the continuation that returns to the main past timeline after the flashback.
items.taskText: 'The inspector arrived at noon. Earlier that morning, a facilities officer had found a leak and had shut off the water. Now, with the inspector beside him, he ___ the damaged pipe.'
items.explanation: Photographed advances the main past scene after the earlier events marked with had; now is the narrative now beside the inspector.

rationales.has photographed: Has photographed changes the reporting center to the present instead of continuing the past scene.
rationales.photographed: Photographed advances the main past scene after the earlier events marked with had; now is the narrative now beside the inspector.
rationales.had photographed: Had photographed keeps the photograph earlier than a past reference point rather than advancing the scene beside the inspector.
rationales.will photograph: Will photograph looks forward from the narrator's present rather than advancing the action in the past scene.

findings: Original repeated a two-hour plan-making duration without adequate context or C1 demand.
audit.microSkill: Returning from past-perfect flashback to simple-past narration
audit.pedagogicalValue: Prevents extending past perfect mechanically after the earlier timeline has ended.
audit.levelReason: Tracking a narrative shift across several sentences is appropriate C1 editing.
audit.similarityNote: A multi-sentence flashback followed by return to the main scene.

items.setupText: Choose the period over which the reported absence of contact is asserted.
items.taskText: At last week's hearing, the manager said, 'We hadn't heard from our former partner since she left the organization.' Nothing is said about contact after the hearing.
options: From the former partner's departure up to the present reading of the report.
Only during the final day before the former partner's departure.
From the former partner's departure up to the past reporting point.
From the hearing until a future return to the organization.
items.answer: From the former partner's departure up to the past reporting point.
items.explanation: The past perfect measures absence of contact from the departure up to the manager's past reporting point; later contact is left open.

rationales.From the former partner's departure up t: Hadn't heard uses a past reference point. The report does not extend the claim through the later period up to now.
rationales.Only during the final day before the for: Since starts the interval at her departure, not on the day before it.
rationales.From the former partner's departure up t: The past perfect measures absence of contact from the departure up to the manager's past reporting point; later contact is left open.
rationales.From the hearing until a future return t: This starts the interval too late and invents a future return that the report does not mention.

findings: Original future-perfect finding item repeated a low-demand form pattern with a valid future-simple alternative.
audit.microSkill: Past-perfect absence bounded by a reporting point
audit.pedagogicalValue: Limits an absence-of-contact claim to the period actually covered by the report.
audit.levelReason: Recovering an implicit endpoint and resisting extension to the present suits C1.
audit.similarityNote: A negative report with an explicitly unknown period after the hearing.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'have completed' in this future eligibility condition.
items.taskText: Applications open next April. If you have completed the trial by then, you can apply for membership.
options: The trial must already be complete at the time this notice is written.
Trial completion must precede the relevant application point next April.
The trial begins after membership has already been granted.
Applicants must be completing the trial while submitting their applications.
items.answer: Trial completion must precede the relevant application point next April.
items.explanation: The present perfect expresses completion relative to a future point supplied by 'by then'; it does not require completion before speech time.

rationales.The trial must already be complete at th: 'By then' points to next April, so completion may still lie in the future from the notice's date.
rationales.The trial begins after membership has al: The condition places completion before application, not after membership is granted.
rationales.Applicants must be completing the trial: 'Have completed' requires reaching completion, rather than merely being in progress at application time.
rationales.Trial completion must precede the releva: The present perfect expresses completion relative to a future point supplied by 'by then'; it does not require completion before speech time.

findings: Original repeated a two-hour teaching duration and did not support an advanced distinction.
audit.microSkill: Perfect anteriority relative to a future conditional point
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates perfect aspect's earlier-than relation from absolute past time.
audit.levelReason: Reading a future reference point across notice sentences is C1 temporal interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: Eligibility at a future date, with completion possibly still future now.

items.setupText: Choose the report that explicitly presents the rule as still valid now.
items.taskText: The receptionist explained the rule yesterday. You are now writing guidance for today's visitors.
options: The receptionist explained that visitors had needed photo identification in 2019.
The receptionist explained that visitors need photo identification.
The receptionist explained that visitors would need photo identification after the rule changed.
The receptionist explained that visitors had been needing photo identification before it was replaced.
items.answer: The receptionist explained that visitors need photo identification.
items.explanation: Keeping need in the present presents the requirement as current, even though the explanation happened yesterday.

rationales.The receptionist explained that visitors: Keeping need in the present presents the requirement as current, even though the explanation happened yesterday.
Had needed in 2019 restricts the claim to an earlier period rather than stating today's requirement.
Would need after a change looks forward from a past viewpoint and does not explicitly identify today's rule.
Before it was replaced locates the requirement in a superseded period, not today's guidance.

findings: Original future-perfect documents item rejected a grammatical will bring and offered only basic form selection.
audit.microSkill: Unbackshifted present for current validity in a past report
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses a deliberate reporting choice to endorse a currently applicable rule.
audit.levelReason: Matching reporting tense to a guidance document's present purpose suits C1.
audit.similarityNote: An editorial choice to assert current validity, not an inference that backshift implies change.

items.setupText: Choose the form explicitly presenting the safety check as complete before tomorrow's opening.
items.taskText: When the venue opens tomorrow, every emergency exit ___ by an independent inspector.
items.explanation: Will have been checked combines future perfect with passive voice to present completed checks before the opening.

rationales.was being checked: Was being checked places a check in progress in the past, without establishing completion before the future opening.
rationales.will have been checked: Will have been checked combines future perfect with passive voice to present completed checks before the opening.
rationales.will be being checked: Will be being checked presents checking as in progress at opening time rather than already complete before it.
rationales.had been checking: Had been checking is active and past; emergency exits are being checked, not carrying out the checks.

findings: Original had been beginning the session for two hours was semantically strained and did not test genuine advanced judgment.
audit.microSkill: Future perfect passive for a required completed state
audit.pedagogicalValue: Coordinates time, completion, and who undergoes an action.
audit.levelReason: A future reference point with passive completion creates C1 structural demand.
audit.similarityNote: Completed safety checks in passive voice, unlike active future milestones.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the distinction between imminent action and actual action.
items.taskText: 'The prospective tenant was about to sign the lease when she noticed the extra fee.'
options: The tenant had signed before she noticed the fee.
The tenant had been signing leases repeatedly before the fee appeared.
The tenant made a new appointment to sign after the fee was removed.
Signing was imminent when she noticed the fee; actual signing is not stated.
items.answer: Signing was imminent when she noticed the fee; actual signing is not stated.
items.explanation: Was about to presents a near-future action from a past viewpoint; the sentence does not establish whether she went on to sign.

rationales.The tenant had signed before she noticed: Was about to sign places signing just ahead of the noticing, not already completed.
rationales.The tenant had been signing leases repea: About to indicates imminence on this occasion, not repeated earlier signing.
rationales.Signing was imminent when she noticed th: Was about to presents a near-future action from a past viewpoint; the sentence does not establish whether she went on to sign.
rationales.The tenant made a new appointment to sig: No later appointment or removal of the fee is reported.

findings: Original future-perfect application item was ambiguous with will complete and repeated the level's formula.
audit.microSkill: Past prospective aspect and non-asserted realization
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids turning an imminent action into a completed event.
audit.levelReason: Distinguishing prospect from realization in a narrative is C1 inference.
audit.similarityNote: An imminent signing interrupted by new information.

items.setupText: Choose the function of 'hear' in this conversational opening.
items.taskText: 'I hear you've accepted the fellowship. Congratulations!'
options: It describes a hearing process occurring continuously during the fellowship.
It makes acceptance conditional on a future announcement.
It reports a sound that the speaker heard before learning any news.
It presents received news as information currently available to the speaker.
items.answer: It presents received news as information currently available to the speaker.
items.explanation: 'I hear' can introduce news the speaker has learned and regards as current; the present form need not describe literal hearing at that instant.

rationales.It describes a hearing process occurring: 'Hear' introduces information here, not an ongoing sensory process during the fellowship.
rationales.It makes acceptance conditional on a fut: "You've accepted" treats acceptance as prior news, not as conditional on a later announcement.
rationales.It reports a sound that the speaker hear: This use of 'hear' concerns learning news, not identifying an earlier sound.
rationales.It presents received news as information: 'I hear' can introduce news the speaker has learned and regards as current; the present form need not describe literal hearing at that instant.

findings: Original repeated a two-hour explanation frame with weak distractors and no C1 interpretation.
audit.microSkill: Present reporting formula with recently received information
audit.pedagogicalValue: Explains present-tense news formulas without a literal-now misreading.
audit.levelReason: Recognizing a discourse-specific use of a common present verb is C1 work.
audit.similarityNote: A conversational evidence formula, separate from historical-present narration.

items.setupText: Choose the pair preserving a future viewed from the narrator's past scene.
items.taskText: In 2010, a weaver took over the workshop. Within five years she ___ it into a cooperative, though she ___ that yet.
items.explanation: Would turn looks forward from 2010; did not know keeps her lack of knowledge at that same past scene.

rationales.would turn / did not know: Would turn looks forward from 2010; did not know keeps her lack of knowledge at that same past scene.
rationales.had turned / will not know: Had turned makes the transformation earlier than 2010, while will not know changes to a future viewpoint from now.
rationales.has turned / does not know: Has turned and does not know shift the reporting center to the present instead of maintaining the past scene.
rationales.turns / had not known: Turns introduces a present narrative form while had not known looks back from a past point, losing the requested shared viewpoint.

findings: Original future-perfect comparison item allowed a simple-future alternative and required little advanced reasoning.
audit.microSkill: Narrator's future in the past with character knowledge
audit.pedagogicalValue: Coordinates later historical outcome with what a character knew at an earlier point.
audit.levelReason: Separating narrator knowledge from a past character viewpoint is C1 narrative control.
audit.similarityNote: A later outcome known to the narrator but unknown in the scene.

items.setupText: Choose the revision that describes repeated recent failures to respond without asserting permanent refusal.
items.taskText: Some messages have received answers, but response has been inconsistent during the past fortnight.
options: The committee secretary had replied to the message before the fortnight began.
The committee secretary will refuse to reply to future messages from now on.
The committee secretary is replying to a message at this very moment.
The committee secretary hasn't been replying consistently to messages lately.
items.answer: The committee secretary hasn't been replying consistently to messages lately.
items.explanation: Hasn't been replying consistently describes a recent pattern across messages while allowing that some did receive replies.

rationales.The committee secretary had replied to t: This reports one earlier completion and says nothing about the recent inconsistent pattern.
rationales.The committee secretary hasn't been repl: Hasn't been replying consistently describes a recent pattern across messages while allowing that some did receive replies.
rationales.The committee secretary will refuse to r: This asserts a future refusal, which goes beyond the evidence of inconsistent recent response.
rationales.The committee secretary is replying to a: A single action in progress now does not summarize the recent pattern across messages.

findings: Original's approving one request for two hours was strained and recycled a low-demand aspect choice.
audit.microSkill: Negative perfect continuous with partial repeated failure
audit.pedagogicalValue: Controls negation scope so inconsistent response is not turned into total non-response.
audit.levelReason: Summarizing a qualified behavioral pattern with precise scope suits C1.
audit.similarityNote: Negative repeated behavior qualified by consistently, with some successful responses preserved.

items.setupText: Choose the analysis that distinguishes the extended pattern from its individual events.
items.taskText: The design studio has been winning small contracts throughout the recovery.
options: The progressive leaves open whether any individual contract has actually been won.
The pattern is viewed as ongoing although individual wins are complete.
The perfect presents the run of wins as finished before the recovery ended.
Replacing has been winning with has won would shift emphasis from results to duration.
items.answer: The pattern is viewed as ongoing although individual wins are complete.
items.explanation: The progressive can organize repeated achievements into an extended pattern without making each individual achievement incomplete.

rationales.The progressive leaves open whether any: Winning contracts reports successful individual wins in this plural achievement reading; the progressive groups them into a pattern.
rationales.The perfect presents the run of wins as: The perfect relates the pattern to the present; it does not establish that the recovery or the run of wins has ended.
rationales.The pattern is viewed as ongoing althoug: The progressive can organize repeated achievements into an extended pattern without making each individual achievement incomplete.
rationales.Replacing has been winning with has won: The proposed shift runs the other way: has won more readily foregrounds achieved contracts, while has been winning foregrounds the developing pattern.

findings: Original described reviewing one report for three years and made the longest future form predictably correct.
audit.microSkill: Iterative interpretation of perfect progressive achievements
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids equating progressive aspect with non-completion of each individual event.
audit.levelReason: Reconciling achievement meaning, plurality, and progressive viewpoint is C2 aspect analysis.
audit.similarityNote: Completed individual wins inside an ongoing aggregate pattern.

items.setupText: Choose the reading that assigns completion to the right event.
items.taskText: Hardly had the appeal begun to be heard when the hearing was adjourned.
options: The appeal had just been heard in full; only the formal adjournment remained.
The appeal was close to being heard, but adjournment prevented the hearing from starting.
The hearing had just started; the appeal's consideration need not have been completed.
The appeal's consideration and the adjournment are both presented as completed before the hearing began.
items.answer: The hearing had just started; the appeal's consideration need not have been completed.
items.explanation: The perfect applies to begun: the start has occurred. Hardly ... when places adjournment soon afterward without making the whole hearing complete.

rationales.The hearing had just started; the appeal: The perfect applies to begun: the start has occurred. Hardly ... when places adjournment soon afterward without making the whole hearing complete.
rationales.The appeal had just been heard in full;: Had begun marks completion of the starting phase, not completion of the appeal's consideration.
rationales.The appeal was close to being heard, but: Hardly had ... begun means the start had just occurred; it does not mean the hearing merely nearly began.
rationales.The appeal's consideration and the adjou: Adjournment follows the start in the main past sequence; it is not inside the earlier event marked by had begun.

findings: Original wrapped simple participle recognition in inversion and gave the same vague feedback to unrelated forms.
audit.microSkill: Perfect scope over a phase verb in hardly inversion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes completing a beginning from completing the larger event begun.
audit.levelReason: Tracking perfect scope through a phase verb and passive infinitive is C2 interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: A completed start embedded within an uncompleted appeal hearing.

items.setupText: Choose the comparison that correctly predicts which continuation is coherent.
items.taskText: A: 'The mason rebuilt the arch during the shutdown.' B: 'The mason was rebuilding the arch during the shutdown.' Consider adding: 'But he abandoned it halfway through.'
options: The continuation fits both equally because past tense leaves completion unasserted.
The continuation fits A more directly because simple past separates activity from its result.
The continuation conflicts with both because the definite object the arch requires a finished result.
The continuation fits B; with A it clashes with the ordinary completed-event reading.
items.answer: The continuation fits B; with A it clashes with the ordinary completed-event reading.
items.explanation: Was rebuilding leaves eventual completion open, so abandonment halfway is coherent. Rebuilt the arch ordinarily asserts the completed event, creating a clash.

rationales.The continuation fits both equally becau: Simple past with rebuilt the arch ordinarily presents the bounded rebuilding as completed, unlike the progressive.
rationales.The continuation fits A more directly be: The simple clause includes the ordinary completion reading; the progressive is the form that leaves the endpoint unasserted.
rationales.The continuation conflicts with both bec: A definite object helps make rebuilding bounded, but progressive aspect can present its internal activity without asserting the endpoint.
rationales.The continuation fits B; with A it clash: Was rebuilding leaves eventual completion open, so abandonment halfway is coherent. Rebuilt the arch ordinarily asserts the completed event, creating a clash.

findings: Original implausibly stretched writing one summary over three years and supplied generic time feedback.
audit.microSkill: Completion commitments tested through narrative continuation
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes lack of a completion assertion from an assertion of non-completion.
audit.levelReason: Testing aspectual commitments against a canceling continuation is C2 semantic editing.
audit.similarityNote: An applied continuation judgment using a bounded construction task.

items.setupText: Choose the analysis that preserves both the inference and the limits of what is inferred.
items.taskText: The newsroom lights were on until dawn. They will have been working through the night, I imagine.
options: The speaker infers that the newsroom's task was completed when the lights went out.
The speaker infers sustained earlier activity without fixing its endpoint.
The speaker predicts that a task will be complete by a future dawn.
The speaker attributes a prior work schedule to the staff without endorsing the activity itself.
items.answer: The speaker infers sustained earlier activity without fixing its endpoint.
items.explanation: Will gives inferential force, the perfect looks back, and the progressive presents sustained work; the sentence does not establish completion or cessation.

rationales.The speaker infers that the newsroom's t: The progressive supports an inference about activity, not a completed task or the exact moment the work stopped.
rationales.The speaker infers sustained earlier act: Will gives inferential force, the perfect looks back, and the progressive presents sustained work; the sentence does not establish completion or cessation.
rationales.The speaker predicts that a task will be: The cited lights provide evidence about the night just ended, so this is retrospective inference rather than a future deadline prediction.
rationales.The speaker attributes a prior work sche: The speaker is drawing a conclusion that work occurred, not merely reporting that someone scheduled it.

findings: Original Hardly item tested only a basic sent participle in an advanced-looking frame.
audit.microSkill: Inferential perfect progressive without an endpoint assertion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates inferred activity from task completion and from a reported plan.
audit.levelReason: Coordinating epistemic force, retrospective aspect, and unasserted cessation is C2 work.
audit.similarityNote: Evidence from a newsroom supports an inference with deliberately limited content.

items.setupText: Choose the update preserving the producer's commitment, including its deadline, while leaving fulfillment unverified.
items.taskText: The producer said, 'We will have edited the soundtrack by Friday.' The editor has no confirmation of the outcome.
options: The producer said the soundtrack would have been edited by Friday.
The producer confirmed that the soundtrack had been edited by Friday.
The producer said the soundtrack would be being edited on Friday.
The producer said the soundtrack would be edited on Friday.
items.answer: The producer said the soundtrack would have been edited by Friday.
items.explanation: Would have been edited preserves the reported future-perfect completion, and by Friday allows earlier completion. Said attributes the commitment without verifying fulfillment.

rationales.The producer confirmed that the soundtra: Confirmed upgrades an attributed commitment to verified completion, which the editor does not have.
rationales.The producer said the soundtrack would b: Would be being edited presents work in progress on Friday rather than completed by the deadline.
rationales.The producer said the soundtrack would h: Would have been edited preserves the reported future-perfect completion, and by Friday allows earlier completion. Said attributes the commitment without verifying fulfillment.
rationales.The producer said the soundtrack would b: On Friday locates the editing on that day; by Friday gives a latest completion point and permits finishing earlier.

findings: Original repeated an artificial three-year list-updating frame and did not require advanced interpretation.
audit.microSkill: Attributed deadline versus exact date, ongoing work, and confirmed completion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves both temporal scope and evidential status in a report of a commitment.
audit.levelReason: Discriminating four grammatical reports with different aspect and attribution is C2 editing.
audit.similarityNote: All alternatives retain Friday and compete on deadline, aspect, and attribution.

items.setupText: Read the final two sentences as the character's unspoken thoughts. Choose the analysis of their viewpoint.
items.taskText: Ruth set down the resignation letter. Tomorrow she would hand it in. Surely that would solve everything.
options: Tomorrow follows Ruth's scene, but would establishes that the resignation was later submitted.
Would makes resignation an unreal alternative that Ruth had already decided against.
The first would belongs to the narrator's forecast, while the second establishes a solution as a historical fact.
Tomorrow follows Ruth's scene, and would can express her projected outcome without verifying it.
items.answer: Tomorrow follows Ruth's scene, and would can express her projected outcome without verifying it.
items.explanation: With the stated character-thought reading, tomorrow is anchored to her scene and would voices what she anticipates; the narrator need not confirm either outcome.

rationales.Tomorrow follows Ruth's scene, and would: With the stated character-thought reading, tomorrow is anchored to her scene and would voices what she anticipates; the narrator need not confirm either outcome.
rationales.Tomorrow follows Ruth's scene, but would: A character's projected action in free indirect thought is not proof of later fulfillment.
rationales.Would makes resignation an unreal altern: Would here can express a future viewed from a past scene, rather than a rejected counterfactual alternative.
rationales.The first would belongs to the narrator': Both projected handing-in and hoped-for solution belong to the character's perspective under the supplied reading, not verified historical outcomes.

findings: Original used Hardly only as decoration around an elementary participle choice.
audit.microSkill: Character-centered future projection in free indirect thought
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates a character's temporal center and expectations from narrator-confirmed events.
audit.levelReason: Reading deictic anchoring and epistemic scope in free indirect discourse suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: A resignation scene interpreted as unspoken thought, not a calendar calculation.

items.setupText: Choose the comparison that respects the speaker's explicitly stated knowledge.
items.taskText: A: 'If the courier was at the depot yesterday, she may have seen the parcel; I don't know whether she was.' B: 'If the courier were here now, she could identify it; she is away.'
options: A leaves seeing the parcel uncertain but establishes presence; B leaves current presence uncertain.
Both conditions establish absence because their verbs have past forms.
A makes past presence counterfactual; B merely expresses uncertainty about current presence.
A leaves past presence open; B imagines a present state contradicted by the context.
items.answer: A leaves past presence open; B imagines a present state contradicted by the context.
items.explanation: Was in A refers to an uncertain past fact. Were in B marks a remote present possibility that the surrounding statement identifies as contrary to fact.

rationales.A leaves seeing the parcel uncertain but: A explicitly withholds knowledge of presence, while B explicitly states that the courier is away.
rationales.A leaves past presence open; B imagines: Was in A refers to an uncertain past fact. Were in B marks a remote present possibility that the surrounding statement identifies as contrary to fact.
rationales.Both conditions establish absence becaus: Past form alone does not establish absence; A is an open question about a past fact.
rationales.A makes past presence counterfactual; B: This reverses the contexts: A leaves presence unknown, whereas B supplies evidence of present absence.

findings: Original's printing one set of forms for three years was artificial and its answer depended on length rather than inference.
audit.microSkill: Temporal past versus remote past in conditions
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes uncertainty about past facts from a contextually counterfactual present.
audit.levelReason: Comparing temporal and modal interpretations using discourse evidence is C2 work.
audit.similarityNote: Keeps the times fixed while alternatives compete on what presence is known or imagined.

items.setupText: Choose the analysis preserving the original condition's status in the later report.
items.taskText: A dispatcher said, 'If the road is open tomorrow, we'll deliver then.' A later report reads, 'The dispatcher said that if the road was open the next day, they would deliver then.'
options: Backshift converts the possible road opening into a condition known not to have been met.
The backshifted forms preserve an open condition and leave its fulfillment unverified.
Would turns the conditional promise into a commitment to deliver regardless of the road's status.
Was preserves uncertainty about delivery but establishes that the road had opened before the original promise.
items.answer: The backshifted forms preserve an open condition and leave its fulfillment unverified.

items.setupText: Choose the reading that correctly relates the eligibility threshold to the ongoing residence.
items.taskText: You move into the district next month. Once you've been living here for six months, you can apply for a residents' parking permit.

Eligibility requires a completed six-month residence followed by departure from the district.
The six months measure the period after application during which residence must continue.
Application and residence begin together, with eligibility confirmed after the six months.
items.answer: Six months must have accumulated before application; residence may continue afterward.
items.explanation: The perfect progressive measures residence up to the future threshold. Completion of that qualifying duration does not require cessation of residence.

rationales.Eligibility requires a completed six-mon: The perfect progressive can reach a duration threshold without ending the residence itself.
rationales.The six months measure the period after: Once makes the accumulated residence a prerequisite for applying, not a period measured after application.
rationales.Six months must have accumulated before: The perfect progressive measures residence up to the future threshold. Completion of that qualifying duration does not require cessation of residence.

items.setupText: Choose the editorial comment that preserves the independent time references in this current article.
items.taskText: The 1970 expedition mapped a glacier that is retreating rapidly.

Mapped requires was retreating, because a relative clause must share its main clause's past viewpoint.
Changing is retreating to has retreated would confine the retreat to the expedition's finished period.
Mapped dates the expedition's work; the relative clause can describe the glacier's condition now.
items.answer: Mapped dates the expedition's work; the relative clause can describe the glacier's condition now.
items.explanation: A relative clause can have its own temporal reference. The article can combine a completed historical mapping with a currently developing retreat.

rationales.Mapped dates the expedition's work; the: A relative clause can have its own temporal reference. The article can combine a completed historical mapping with a currently developing retreat.
rationales.Is retreating shifts mapped into a histo: The relative clause does not change the past-tense reference of mapped.
rationales.Mapped requires was retreating, because: Tense in a relative clause need not be mechanically backshifted with the main clause; was retreating would supply a past rather than current viewpoint.
rationales.Changing is retreating to has retreated: Has retreated would look back from a present reference point, not automatically restrict retreat to the expedition's year.

items.setupText: Choose the analysis that separates the asserted events from a defeasible result inference.
items.taskText: The caretaker has opened the window twice today, but it is closed now.

The perfect asserts a current open state, so the closing clause retracts the two opening events.
Today's unfinished time span makes the two individual openings unfinished activities.
The perfect asserts only present evidence for the openings, leaving their occurrence uncommitted.
items.answer: The opening events are complete; their resulting state need not persist.
items.explanation: Twice counts completed openings in today's reporting period. Neither event must still have an open window as its current result.

rationales.The perfect asserts a current open state: A later closing can reverse the result without retracting the earlier opening events; this use of the perfect counts events.

items.setupText: Choose the explanation that identifies the relevant period for each verb.
items.taskText: Although the novelist died in 1920, her work has influenced generations of translators and continues to do so.
options: The perfect requires the influence to be confined to translators who met the novelist.
The perfect closes the influence period, and continues introduces a separate new influence period.
Died closes the life period; the work's influence extends to the present.
The perfect attributes continuing personal activity to the novelist despite the dated death.
items.answer: Died closes the life period; the work's influence extends to the present.
items.explanation: The death and the influence concern different subjects and temporal spans. A closed authorial lifetime does not close the work's history of effects.

rationales.The perfect requires the influence to be: The work can influence later readers indirectly, so personal contact and overlapping lifetimes are not required.

items.setupText: Choose the comparison that avoids inventing a stopping date or an uninterrupted single event.
items.taskText: A: 'By May, I will have run the night-bus service for a decade.' B: 'By May, I will have been running the night-bus service for a decade.'
options: A makes May the service's stopping date, while B states that the service continues afterward.
A can summarize accrued tenure; B foregrounds ongoing operation, without either fixing a stopping date.
B places the start of the decade at May, while A places its completion there.
B describes one uninterrupted act of running a bus, whereas A permits repeated nightly operations.
items.answer: A can summarize accrued tenure; B foregrounds ongoing operation, without either fixing a stopping date.
items.explanation: The simple perfect can summarize accumulated operation, while the progressive highlights its ongoing character. Neither wording independently schedules its end.

rationales.A can summarize accrued tenure; B foregr: The simple perfect can summarize accumulated operation, while the progressive highlights its ongoing character. Neither wording independently schedules its end.

audit.similarityNote: Two valid accounts of a decade operating a recurring night service.

items.setupText: Choose the revision unambiguously measuring a ten-year absence rather than the duration of residence.
items.taskText: The draft reads, 'At the reunion, Amir hadn't lived in the town for ten years.' The intended meaning is that his last residence ended ten years before the reunion.
options: At the reunion, Amir had not yet completed ten years of living in the town.
At the reunion, Amir had lived in the town for less than ten years in total.
At the reunion, it had been ten years since Amir last lived in the town.
At the reunion, Amir had left the town ten years after first moving there.
items.answer: At the reunion, it had been ten years since Amir last lived in the town.
items.explanation: Ten years since he last lived there explicitly measures the interval after residence ended, removing the scope ambiguity.

rationales.At the reunion, it had been ten years si: Ten years since he last lived there explicitly measures the interval after residence ended, removing the scope ambiguity.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Clarifies whether a duration measures residence or time without residence.

items.setupText: Choose the analysis preserving the uncertainty expressed by the follow-up question.
items.taskText: I thought you were leaving tomorrow. Has the booking changed?
options: An earlier belief concerned a later arrangement whose status is now being checked.
Thought establishes that the speaker now regards the arrangement as canceled.
Tomorrow prevents were leaving from being backshifted, so it must express an unreal condition.
Were leaving locates departure in progress when the earlier belief was formed.
items.answer: An earlier belief concerned a later arrangement whose status is now being checked.
items.explanation: Thought anchors an earlier belief; were leaving reports a future arrangement from that viewpoint. The question checks rather than settles its current status.

rationales.Thought establishes that the speaker now: A past belief may be tentatively distanced, but the question does not establish that the booking has been canceled.
rationales.An earlier belief concerned a later arra: Thought anchors an earlier belief; were leaving reports a future arrangement from that viewpoint. The question checks rather than settles its current status.

items.setupText: Choose the editorial analysis appropriate to an enthusiastic informal travel diary.
items.taskText: I'm loving the quieter pace here, though I expect I'll miss the city soon.

The progressive confines enjoyment to the exact moment when the diary entry is being written.

items.setupText: Which analysis best accounts for the sequence of verb forms?
items.taskText: During each harvest season, the miller would start work at dawn. By then the growers would have weighed their grain, and the carts would be waiting outside.
options: Would have presents each weighing as a contemplated alternative to the growers' actual routine.
Would have predicts, from each dawn, a completed weighing still ahead in that day's routine.
Would have backshifts an earlier promise by the growers to complete the weighing on each occasion.
Completed weighings precede the starts of work within a recurring past pattern.

items.setupText: Choose the editorial comment that preserves the force of a timetable statement.
items.taskText: The last ferry leaves at nine. Tonight's sailing may be canceled because of fog.

Changing leaves to will have left at nine would preserve the same schedule claim while making it more formal.

Changing leaves to was due to leave would preserve the current viewpoint while merely reducing certainty.
items.answer: The present form states the schedule; uncertainty about sailing does not erase that schedule.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation preserving the perfect infinitive's reference point and the nonfactual status of a hope.
items.taskText: Work has not started. The engineers hope to have stabilized the sea wall before the winter tides arrive.
options: The perfect makes stabilization earlier than the expression of hope, so the first sentence conflicts with it.
Completion is projected before the tides, not necessarily before the hope is expressed.
The perfect makes completion an established fact, even though hope leaves its desirability uncertain.
Replacing to have stabilized with to stabilize would rule out completion before the tides.
items.answer: Completion is projected before the tides, not necessarily before the hope is expressed.
items.explanation: To have stabilized presents the desired result as complete before a future boundary. Hope does not assert that this desired completion will occur.

rationales.The perfect makes stabilization earlier: The perfect infinitive can take a future reference point supplied by the tides; it does not force stabilization to precede the present hope.
rationales.Completion is projected before the tides: To have stabilized presents the desired result as complete before a future boundary. Hope does not assert that this desired completion will occur.

rationales.Replacing to have stabilized with to sta: To stabilize before the tides can also express timely completion. The perfect explicitly adds a retrospective completed-result perspective, not an exclusive ability to meet a deadline.
